name: Highborne Relic (Classic)
summary: In Darkshore, Highborne Relics remain in the hands of spirits haunting Ameth'Aran. Night elf scholars seek them for destruction before their dormant magic can cause more harm.

sections.title: Remnants of the Sundering
sections.body: Ten thousand years ago, the Highborne caste brought ruin upon ancient Kalimdor through reckless arcane magic. Their estates lie in shattered ruins across Darkshore. At Ameth'Aran, wailing apparitions wander among the crumbling columns, still clutching the implements of their old sorcery. The relics bind arcane taint to the spirits, who will not release the objects tied to their undoing.

sections.title: Purging the Arcane Taint
sections.body: Night elf society largely renounced arcane magic after the Great Sundering, and scholars see these relics as a grave hazard. Acting on reports from the Sentinels, Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine sends travelers to wrest them from the cursed spirits. Once gathered, the relics are destroyed so the Highborne's ancient evils and catastrophic mistakes cannot be repeated.

faq.q: Where do Highborne Relics come from?
aliases: where do i find highborne relics
faq.answer: The spirits haunting Ameth'Aran carry Highborne Relics among the ancient ruins east of the main road in southern Darkshore. The wailing ghosts clutch them among the stones.

faq.q: Why does Thundris Windweaver want these relics?
faq.answer: Thundris Windweaver fears the arcane corruption clinging to the relics. He gathers them for destruction, so no one can revive the dangerous Highborne sorcery.

faq.q: Why are the Highborne spirits still in Ameth'Aran?
faq.answer: The spirits are ancient Highborne nobility who perished when the world shattered ten thousand years ago. Their restless souls remain bound to the ruins of their former city, cursed by their hubris and attachment to arcane magic.

faq.q: Are Highborne Relics safe to use?
faq.answer: No. Night elves consider the relics tainted by the unchecked arcane practices that triggered the Great Sundering. Their dormant magic is hazardous, so scholars demand their destruction instead of study.

angles.text: For night elves, these relics recall the arcane arrogance that tore their ancient civilization apart.
As a mage, you may find the relics' arcane craftsmanship fascinating. The local night elf authorities insist they be destroyed.
